<<easyJet’s profits slide amid Brexit fallout>>

Section 1  
easyJet reported a sharp drop in annual profits as the airline faced pressure from Brexit-related currency swings and weaker fares. Pre-tax profits fell 17% to £408m, down from £494m, even as passenger numbers reached a record 80.2 million. The carrier said revenues topped £5bn, but lower ticket prices were needed to fill more seats on fuller aircraft. Carolyn McCall described the year as difficult for aviation, while saying the airline’s focus on strong airport positions, efficient service, and disciplined cost control had helped it stay ahead while rivals struggled.

Section 2  
A major blow came from the pound’s slump after the referendum, which added £101m in costs despite cheaper fuel in dollar terms. easyJet also said it would need to adjust its ownership rules to ensure it remains majority owned and controlled by EU nationals after 2019. Around a third of the company is held by founder Stelios Haji-Ioannou, whose dual UK-Cypriot nationality means his stake will be treated as EU-owned. The airline plans to ask shareholders at its 2018 AGM for powers to require UK investors to sell if needed so it can continue flying freely across Europe.

Section 3  
Investors reacted positively, sending shares up more than 5% in early trading as the company pointed to strong forward bookings and improving revenue in the new financial year. easyJet said part of the boost was due to capacity leaving the market, creating room for its own growth. In a business where firms must dare to adapt, the airline’s leaders framed the changes as practical rather than dramatic, a necessary treat for long-term stability. Even as competition shifts like a fishing net in rough seas, easyJet hopes its position at major airports will help it remain a leading force in the wider society of European air travel.
